text:
Alex Formenton is back in the NHL for the first time since 2021-22. Edmonton signed him to a one-year deal in September after his years playing in Switzerland, and the signing drew heavy criticism: he was one of five players from Canada's 2018 world junior team charged with sexual assault and found not guilty in July 2025.

On the ice, the case for him was speed and penalty killing, and the speed is real: his top skating speed ranks in the 98th percentile of the league. The rest has been hard going. He has five points in 21 games, and his minutes have dropped by more than two and a half a night over the last ten, down to 9.1 and 9.4 in the last two games. At five on five Edmonton has taken just 34% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on the ice, about 17 points worse than without him. If anything, the goals have flattered that line: the Oilers have scored well above what their chances deserve while he plays.
headline: Alex Formenton's NHL return, by the numbers so far
